newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open down 3.00 to 5.00 cents.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open down 3.00 to 5.00 cents.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 3.00 to 5.00 cents lower Friday in a technical correction to the market's recent explosive rally, traders said.
But some traders said a further drawdown in exchange stockpiles was likely to keep prices closer to unchanged at the opening.
"It's due five lower, but I'm going to call it unchanged," one trader said. "We had certifieds down and that's bullish."
After Thursday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 4,000 bags, to 43,668 bags as of April 30.
However, there were 7,227 bags of coffee pending grading, the exchange said.

Thursday, New York arabica futures surged to new life-of-contract highs as continued supply woes fueled speculative buying. July coffee ended up 12.50 cents at 222.90 cents a lb after trading from a new high of 224.00 to 210.00.
Spot May, which expires in 2-1/2 weeks, settled up 13.70 at 252.05 after setting a new contract high of 255.00 cents -- its highest intraday level since July 1994.
The May/July switch, a barometer of nearby availability, widened to 29.85 from 28.65 at the close on Wednesday.
Technically, July resistance was seen at 225.00, while support was pegged at 211.75.
On the fundamental front, German roaster Tchibo Frisch-Roest Kaffee said on Friday it has raised its retail prices by up by one mark per 500 grams, effective immediately.

LIFFE coffee futures were firmer early Friday, but well below pre-opening expectations. London was called a hefty $100-$120 higher on numbers after New York's sharp rally on Thursday, but LIFFE July managed to gap just $29 at the open. By the midday break, July was up only $2, at $1,662.
